identity.title: Toolkit-free rich editor state and text input

closure_unit.outcome: The rich editor's document, selection, history, composition, embed and draft state live in small toolkit-free crates that the egui widget and the new shell both consume, with no behaviour lost.

materialized_acceptance.text: Closure: the rich-editor state crates compile without egui, eframe, egui-winit, egui-wgpu, egui_tiles, epaint, ecolor, emath, egui_kittest, kumihimo-egui, cabinet-egui, cabinet-peak-egui, handshake_context_menu_egui, wgpu, wgpu-core, wgpu-hal, glow and have no painter, galley, response or context type in any signature.

Every rich-editor feature keeps its behaviour: blocks, inline marks, tables and lists where present, wikilinks, transclusion, embeds and CKC drops, slash commands, properties, find/replace, daily notes, reading mode, outline, markdown projection, drafts and save recovery. The parity list names file and test per feature.
The egui widget consumes the extracted state and shrinks; document, selection, history and draft state exist once.

IME: the semantics of ime_handler.rs handle_ime_event run on the same toolkit-free event type as the code editor; preedit never enters the document; commit inserts once at the anchor, updates undo and caret; composition state stays with Kumihimo.
Layout requests (line breaks, block bounds, caret pixels, bidi, fallback) are expressed as data and answered by the Kumihimo text port; the crates contain no shaping code.
Drafts, save, conflict and recovery keep their on-disk formats and their refusal behaviour on stale revisions; the existing test count does not fall.
Embed views keep a toolkit-free model (handshake_embed_views is egui-bound today); the view half moves to the new UI layer only through the asset adapter.
Reusable mechanics missing in handshake_rich_document_model, handshake_rich_formatting, handshake_find_replace, handshake_wikilink_semantics or handshake_embed_views go to MT-198 first.

implementation_steps.step: S1 (first coding slice): document_state crate. Bind the document handle, revision, history and draft identity that have no toolkit type; list every widget field with its owner and toolkit type; egui widget keeps compiling.
S2: selection crate: block and text selection, caret anchors, word motion over the asset mechanics.
S3: composition crate: preedit anchor, commit and cancel mapping over the shared event type; port tests from ime_handler.rs; composition state stays with Kumihimo.
S4: layout_requests crate: what the view must know (blocks, spans, embeds, caret queries) as data.
S5: embed_model crate: embed identity, states (loading, missing, denied, error) and drop contracts without a view.
S6: drafts crate and shrink rich_editor_widget.rs; parity list complete.

hbr_obligations.obligation_or_reason: Surface mounts only in the kernel-owned Vulkan shell; no toolkit type in a public contract; asset-local hosts are not acceptance.
Each control and action declared once with a stable id that feeds GUI, AccessKit, Argus and UserManual.
No GPU work in the state crates.
Every cache, queue and buffer bounded and accounted, with overload, cancel, stale-revision and release behaviour.
GUI actions, states, errors and GPU failures through the existing internal_diagnostics allowlist, content-free.
Survival with the pane mounted is MT-202 AC202-9.
Every command carries actor/session, command id, revision and correlation; correlation grants nothing.
Focus, IME, keyboard and truthful states; docking is MT-200.
Validator drives the running surface through Argus (stable author_id, no foreground).
Renderer error scan on every captured frame: Vulkan validation messages and runtime errors; any error fails.
Capture matrix: normal, constrained viewport, and empty/error/loading/multi-item states.
Trace projection where there is no direct surface.
A surface Argus cannot see or steer is repaired in this MT or recorded as a blocking gap.
Automated runs use a quiet, never-activated window or offscreen frame; zero focus or Z-order change.
No OS input injection, cursor movement or foregrounding on any path, tests included.
Background launches record owner and are reclaimed; no orphan windows or processes.
A step that needs the foreground (real OS IME typing) is declared first and run by the Operator.
Three-tier diagnostic outcome recorded per tier (hbr_int_009_tier_obligations).
One owning module in execution.module_ref; write scope derives from its roots; dependency direction stated.
Warm rebuild time and relinked test binaries recorded for the candidate.
Mechanic consumed from its single existing owner (context_capsule.consumed_capability_refs).
No new canonical mechanic without a spec primitive and an owner search.
Accountable owner and independently selectable source, dependency, build, test and artifact closure.
Exact embedding adapter; host policy stays in Handshake.
Asset change lands in its canonical repository and is re-read before any host write.
Missing shared logic is added to the asset first; no host workaround, copy or fork.
Scope linkage preserved on every projected resource.
Default deny kept for missing, stale or revoked context at every boundary touched.
Concurrent accounts see neither content nor existence metadata of each other.
Logout, switch or revocation clears or fences caches, captures, snapshots and stale UI state.
Concurrent agents plus Operator edits: no silent last-writer-wins; conflicts are typed.
Cargo target under the one artifact root, owner-scoped, named in the dispatch (KB-OUT-008).
Owner cleans only its own scoped artifact folder.
UserManual updated in the same change; MANUAL_VERSION bumped where declared.
A no-context model can operate the surface from the manual alone.
Manual entries are code-truthful and self-consistency tested.
